turns.t: Hello, doctor. I'm Maya, I'm Mr Okafor's carer, I drove him in. He's got a sore lower back since he helped move his daughter's house on the weekend. ~
Thanks for bringing him, Maya. Mr Okafor, how are you? ~
Sore, doctor. Right across my lower back. I lifted a lot of boxes.
When did it begin?
Saturday afternoon, after the sofa. It's Monday now.
Is it a dull ache or sharp? ~
A dull ache, but sharp when I bend. ~
Does it go anywhere? ~
No. Just the back. ~
Let me have a feel. Can you stand up for me?
Slowly. ~
There's tenderness in the muscles on both sides of the lower back, and they feel tight.
That's where it hurts. ~
He's been walking about all morning, doctor. ~
That's good. Mr Okafor, does anyone in your family have back trouble?
My mother had a bad back all her life.
That's useful to know. Here's what I'd advise. Keep moving, short gentle walks, little and often.
I thought I should rest. ~
Bed rest makes it worse. Gentle movement helps it recover. ~
That's what the physio told his sister. ~
Use a hot water bottle on the sore area, for twenty minutes at a time.
Warm, not hot. ~
Exactly. And avoid heavy lifting for two weeks, even a bag of shopping.
I'll carry the shopping. ~
That's a relief. ~
Sleep on your side with a pillow between your knees.
I'll try. ~
Most back pain like this settles in a couple of weeks. ~
That's good to hear. ~
If it hasn't improved in two weeks, or if you get any weakness in your legs, come back and see me.
I'll watch for that. ~
Thank you, doctor. ~
Take care. ~
